name: Apollo 11 Lunar Module Descent Stage
blueprintTitle: LUNAR MODULE DESCENT STAGE // QUADRANT & PROPULSION ANATOMY

components.name: Descent Propulsion System (DPS)
components.description: A pioneering throttleable rocket engine delivering 4,400 N to 43,900 N of thrust using hypergolic propellants (Aerozine-50 and Nitrogen Tetroxide). Enabled Neil Armstrong to manually hover and navigate past boulders in West Crater.
components.materials: Niobium-alloy nozzle extension, titanium propellant tanks

components.name: Crushable Honeycomb Landing Struts
components.description: Four cantilevered landing legs with aluminum honeycomb cartridges designed to compress on impact, absorbing landing shock. Footpads were 94 cm in diameter to prevent sinking into lunar dust.
components.materials: Aluminized Mylar thermal wrap, crushable aluminum honeycomb

components.name: Lunar Surface Sensing Probes
components.description: Three 1.7-meter flexible probe wires extending below the footpads. When they touched the lunar regolith, they triggered the blue 'LUNAR CONTACT' light on the control panel, instructing the commander to shut off the engine.
components.materials: Tempered spring steel

components.name: Modular Equipment Stowage Assembly (MESA)
components.description: Located in Quadrant IV, this hinged pallet dropped down when Armstrong pulled a lanyard on the porch. It housed the Westinghouse black-and-white TV camera that broadcast his first steps to 650 million viewers on Earth.
components.materials: Structural magnesium and thermal blankets

components.name: Multi-Layer Kapton & Mylar Foil Blankets
components.description: Up to 25 layers of aluminized Mylar and amber Kapton film. Designed to reflect intense solar radiation (up to +120°C in sunlight) and retain internal heat during lunar shadow (-130°C).
components.materials: Gold Kapton, aluminized Mylar, Inconel foil

components.name: EASEP Scientific Experiment Bay
components.description: Quadrant II housed the Early Apollo Surface Experiments Package: the Laser Ranging Retroreflector (LRRR) that scientists still ping today and the Passive Seismic Experiment Package (PSEP).
components.materials: Fused silica corner-cube prisms in aluminum housing

name: Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle
blueprintTitle: LUNAR ROVING VEHICLE // CHASSIS, TRACTION & AVIONICS

components.name: Woven Wire Mesh Tires
components.description: Because rubber tires would burst or freeze in the lunar vacuum, the wheels were crafted from zinc-coated steel piano wire with titanium chevron treads riveted to the exterior for traction in powdery regolith.
components.materials: 0.84 mm zinc-coated steel wire, titanium chevrons

components.name: T-Handle Flight Controller
components.description: Instead of a steering wheel or pedals, the rover was driven with a single T-shaped joystick between the seats. Tilting forward accelerated, pulling back applied mechanical brakes, and tilting left/right commanded 4-wheel steering.
components.materials: Machined aluminum with glove-grip contours

components.name: High-Gain Umbrella Dish Antenna
components.description: A collapsible 0.9-meter wire-mesh parabolic reflector. Astronauts aimed it directly at Earth using an optical sight to send back real-time color television and biomedical telemetry.
components.materials: Gold-plated molybdenum wire mesh

components.name: Dual 36-Volt Silver-Zinc Batteries
components.description: Two 36-volt non-rechargeable silver-zinc potassium hydroxide batteries located in the forward chassis. They powered four independent 0.25-horsepower traction motors located inside each wheel hub.
components.materials: Silver-zinc alkaline cells (121 Ah capacity)

components.name: Ground-Controlled Color TV Assembly (GCTA)
components.description: Mounted on the forward deck, this color television camera was operated remotely by Ed Fendell at Mission Control in Houston. It tracked astronaut EVAs and captured the famous Apollo 17 lunar module liftoff.
components.materials: Vidicon tube with motorized zoom, pan, and tilt gimbal

name: Viking 1 Lander
blueprintTitle: VIKING 1 LANDER // BIOLOGY SUITE & METEOROLOGY SCHEMATIC

components.name: Automated Biology Experiment Suite (GCMS)
components.description: A 0.03 m³ biological mini-laboratory housing three biology experiments (Pyrolytic Release, Labeled Release, Gas Exchange) and a Gas Chromatograph Mass Spectrometer that baked soil samples to test for organic molecules.
components.materials: Titanium ovens, radioactive carbon-14 tracers, krypton valves

components.name: Surface Sampler Collector Arm
components.description: A motorized 3-meter boom that extended like a steel tape measure. It featured a backhoe collector scoop, temperature sensor, and vibrator sieve to dig trenches and deliver soil into the onboard analytical ovens.
components.materials: Beryllium-copper alloy retractable tube, stainless steel scoop

components.name: Dual SNAP-19 Radioisotope Generators (RTG)
components.description: Two SNAP-19 RTGs encased in beryllium heat shields. Powered by the radioactive decay of Plutonium-238, they supplied 57 watts of continuous electrical power and waste heat to survive frigid Martian nights.
components.materials: Plutonium-238 dioxide capsules, lead-telluride thermocouples

components.name: Meteorology Sensor Boom
components.description: Mounted on an upright boom to avoid spacecraft engine heat, it measured Martian atmospheric temperature, wind speed, wind direction, and atmospheric pressure (averaging 7.5 millibars).
components.materials: Hot-film anemometer, platinum resistance thermometers

components.name: Dual Facsimile Panoramic Cameras
components.description: Two nodding-mirror cameras that scanned the landscape line-by-line, capturing the first historic color images of the Martian surface, showing red sky and rusty orange rocks in Chryse Planitia.
components.materials: Silicon photodiode array with motorized mirror drive

components.name: 6-Wheel Rocker-Bogie Suspension
components.description: A differential rocker-bogie mechanism connecting 6 aluminum wheels without springs. Allowed the 11.5 kg rover to climb over rocks larger than its 13-cm wheels while keeping the main computer body stable.
components.materials: Machined titanium and aluminum chassis tubing

components.name: Alpha Particle X-Ray Spectrometer (APXS)
components.description: Mounted on a deployment arm at the rear. Pressed directly against rocks like 'Barnacle Bill' and 'Yogi' to irradiate them with Curium-244, revealing high silica volcanic andesite composition.
components.materials: Curium-244 radioactive source, silicon detector diode

components.name: Gallium Arsenide Solar Array Deck
components.description: A 0.22 m² flat array of high-efficiency gallium arsenide solar cells generating approximately 16 watts of peak power at Martian noon, supplemented by primary non-rechargeable lithium thionyl chloride batteries.
components.materials: Gallium arsenide on germanium substrate

components.name: Laser Hazard Detection Stripers
components.description: Five diode lasers projected horizontal laser stripes on the ground ahead. The forward stereo CCD cameras measured curvature in the stripes to spot drop-offs and boulders autonomously.
components.materials: Infrared laser diodes (820 nm wavelength)

components.name: 80C85 Rad-Hard Microprocessor
components.description: An 8-bit radiation-hardened Intel 80C85 processor running at 2 MHz with 512 KB RAM and 176 KB flash ROM. Managed autonomous obstacle avoidance, wheel drive motors, and communication with the Pathfinder lander.
components.materials: Silicon-on-sapphire radiation-hardened integrated circuit

name: Mars Pathfinder Lander
blueprintTitle: PATHFINDER LANDER // PETAL DEPLOYMENT & AIRBAG CHASSIS

components.name: Triangular Self-Righting Petals
components.description: Three hinged triangular solar petals surrounding a central base. High-torque electric actuators drove the petals downward with enough force to roll the landed spacecraft upright onto its base regardless of how it bounced.
components.materials: Graphite-epoxy composite honeycomb core

components.name: 24-Lobe Kevlar Airbag Cluster
components.description: Four interconnected sets of six airbags inflated with cool-gas generators 8 seconds before touchdown, allowing the lander to survive a 14 m/s impact and bounce over 15 times across the rocky terrain of Ares Vallis.
components.materials: Multi-layer Vectran / Kevlar fabric with abrasion covers

components.name: Imager for Mars Pathfinder (IMP)
components.description: Mounted atop a 80-cm pop-up mast, the IMP camera featured stereo optics separated by 14 cm (mimicking human eyes) with 12 optical filters to capture 3D multi-spectral panoramas and monitor atmospheric dust.
components.materials: Charge-coupled device (CCD) array with motorized filter wheel

components.name: Deployable Rover Egress Ramps
components.description: Dual deployable fabric and metal ramps that unfurled over the deflated airbags, giving Sojourner a smooth incline to roll down from the lander deck onto the Martian soil.
components.materials: Vectran fabric with guide rails and tension springs

name: Voyager 1 Spacecraft
blueprintTitle: VOYAGER 1 // INTERSTELLAR ANTENNA, RTG & GOLDEN RECORD

components.name: 3.7-Meter High-Gain Reflector (HGA)
components.description: A 3.7-meter parabolic aluminum dish antenna. Focuses ultra-faint 20-watt microwave signals into a narrow 0.5-degree beam directed continuously back at Earth across more than 24 billion kilometers.
components.materials: Graphite-epoxy honeycomb reflector with gold feed horn

components.name: Voyager Golden Record & Cover
components.description: A 12-inch gold-plated copper phonograph record protected by an electroplated aluminum jacket with an ultra-pure Uranium-238 radioactivity clock. Carries 115 images, greetings in 55 languages, and natural Earth sounds.
components.materials: Gold-plated copper disc, aluminum cover, nickel-plated stylus

components.name: 3 Multihundred-Watt RTGs (Nuclear Power)
components.description: Three MHW-RTGs mounted on a deployable boom. Converting heat from Plutonium-238 decay into electricity, they originally produced 470 watts of power and still supply ~220 watts after 48+ continuous years in space.
components.materials: Silicon-germanium thermocouples, beryllium radiation shield

components.name: 13-Meter Magnetometer Boom
components.description: A 13-meter deployable triangular fiberglass boom that held high-sensitivity fluxgate magnetometers far away from the spacecraft's electrical wiring. In 2012, it detected the dramatic shift into interstellar magnetic fields.
components.materials: Coiled fiberglass lattice mast with triaxial fluxgate sensors

components.name: Plasma Wave Subsystem (PWS) Dipole Antennas
components.description: Two 10-meter beryllium copper antenna rods forming a V-shape. They recorded electron plasma oscillations, proving in August 2012 that electron density had spiked by a factor of 40—confirming entry into interstellar space.
components.materials: Spring-loaded beryllium copper tubular antennas
